newsitem.title: USA: Executive says Huang tried to mask funds - report.
newsitem.headline: Executive says Huang tried to mask funds - report.

text.p: An executive of an Asian-American business group said he was approached by fund-raiser John Huang and asked to funnel more than $250,000 through members as contributions to the Democratic National Committee in return for a $45,000 payment, the Washington Post reported on Thursday.

Rawlein Soberano, vice president of the Fairfax, Virginia-based Asian American Business Roundtable, told the newspaper there was no discussion of where the money was to have come from and said he rejected Huang's offer immediately.
"I said no. I knew when you do this kind of thing, it's no different from laundering money from the drug lords," Soberano said in an interview.
The Post said that Huang, through an attorney who declined to be quoted by name, denied making the proposal to Soberano last summer.
"Mr. Huang would never have said anything other than that we need your help," the attorney was quoted as saying. "The rest did not happen."

Soberano's account was the first direct allegation that Huang, whose fund-raising activities among Asian Americans are under investigation, tried to hide the source of campaign contributions to the DNC and enlist the help of others in falsely reporting the origins of large donations, the newspaper said.
A Justice Department task force is investigating Huang in connection with possible illegal campaign contributions from foreign sources.
Huang raised about $3.4 million for the Democrats' 1996 campaign, almost half of which has since been returned by the DNC because of questions about its source.

In a separate report, the Post said that a twice-convicted felon who met with Presdent Bill Clinton at one of the small controversial White House coffee sessions in 1995 appeared on four other occasions at DNC fund-raising events with Clinton last year.

Eric Wynn was convicted in 1995 of criminal securities fraud that benefited a member of an organized crime family and also served two years in prison after a 1989 guilty plea on theft and tax charges.

The Post, quoting records and interviews with DNC officials, said Wynn attended a March 9 fund-raiser in California where he had his picture taken with Clinton; a $25,000-a-person dinner with Clinton in Coral Gables, Florida, on April 29; the 50th birthday party for the president at New York's Radio City Music Hall on Aug. 18; and a $12,500-a-person dinner for Clinton in Beverly Hills, California, on Sept. 12.

The newspaper reported that at the March 9 event witnesses said Wynn, who has been trying to win a pardon, spoke with Clinton in the presence of his attorney Richard Mays, who is a longtime friend of the president's.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry told the Post Clinton recalled "no substantive private meeting with Mr. Wynn and is certain he never entertained any discussion of Mr. Wynn's legal situation."
